deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is an archival receipt or inventory note headed: "Schumachers Briefe an Gauss, welche aus dem handschriftlichen Nachlass von Gauss an Peters in Altona verliehen worden sind. Göttingen 1857. Jan. 24." In English: Schumacher's letters to Gauss which were lent from Gauss's manuscript estate to Peters in Altona, Göttingen, 24 January 1857.

The letters are listed in 32 fascicles (Hefte):
- Heft 1: 61 letters, 1808–1819.
- Hefte 2–32: one fascicle per year, 1820 to 1850.
- Yearly counts in order: 5, 15, 8, 18, 23, 18, 18, 19, 17, 10, 11, 15, 8, 8, 18, 19, 35, 20, 14, 31, 32, 18, 29, 36, 58, 51, 62, 55, 17, 21, 33.

The stated total is "Summa: 803 Briefe von 1808 bis 1850." A note adds that Peters also received 5 letters of his own to Gauss, from 1853 and 1854.

The only computation on the page is this sum. Adding the 32 entries as read from the image gives 803 exactly, so the stated total checks.

Context (my addition): Gauss died in 1855 and H. C. Schumacher in 1850. C. A. F. Peters, Schumacher's successor at Altona, edited the published Gauss–Schumacher correspondence (6 vols., 1860–65). The letters were lent to him for that edition. This explains why the list ends in 1850 and why Peters's own 1853–54 letters were added. The page shows only that the note was filed among the papers in the Riemann bundle. Attributing the hand to Riemann is unsure: it may be an administrative note by whoever handled Gauss's Nachlass at Göttingen.
errors: None. The 32 fascicle counts as read from the image (61 + 5 + 15 + ... + 21 + 33) sum to exactly 803, matching the stated Summa.

results.what: Inventory and receipt of 803 letters from Schumacher to Gauss (1808–1850, in 32 fascicles), plus 5 letters from Peters to Gauss (1853–54), lent from Gauss's Nachlass to C. A. F. Peters in Altona, dated Göttingen, 24 January 1857.
results.modern_name: Archival record / loan list; background to the edition 'Briefwechsel zwischen C. F. Gauss und H. C. Schumacher' (ed. C. A. F. Peters, 1860–65)
results.usually_credited_to: Not applicable (administrative document); the edition is credited to C. A. F. Peters

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely administrative bookkeeping about Gauss's correspondence, with no mathematical content. Its only mild interest is as a document on the handling of Gauss's Nachlass in Göttingen in 1857 and on the preparation of the Gauss–Schumacher edition. Whether it is even in Riemann's hand is uncertain.

checkable.asserts: The fascicle counts as read from the image add up to the stated total of 803 letters.
There are 32 fascicles: Heft 1 covers 1808–1819, and Hefte 2–32 cover the 31 years 1820–1850.
One fascicle per year from 1820 to 1850 gives 31 fascicles, which together with Heft 1 makes 32.

transcription_corrections: The machine transcription of this page agrees with the image; it correctly reads 'verliehen' and 'Jan. 24'.
The 'next page' transcription is a mirror-reversed show-through of this same text, so its variants are misreadings. 'übersendet' should be 'verliehen'.
Further show-through misreadings: 'Jan. 20' should be 'Jan. 24', and '3 Briefe von Peters' should be '5 Briefe'.

Further show-through count errors, corrected from the image of this page: 1823 is 18 (not 11), 1825 is 18 (not 13), 1832 is 8 (not 6), 1844 is 58 (not 35), 1847 is 55 (not 53), and 1849 is 21 (not 27). Only the counts from this page sum to 803.
'Gauss' is written with the long-s/ß ligature ('Gauſs'/'Gauß') in the manuscript.
